title: Screen Guild Theater
paragraphs: A Hollywood anthology in which major film stars performed condensed radio versions of movies and other dramatic stories, with the program closely associated with fundraising for the Motion Picture Relief Fund.
Hollywood dramatic anthology built around condensed performances/adaptations of motion pictures and related dramatic material. GRH contains 364 dated recordings through June 1, 1952.

GRH documents the program through CBS initial era (January 8, 1939 to June 28, 1948) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], NBC/Camel era (October 7, 1948 to June 29, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], ABC hour era (September 7, 1950 to May 31, 1951) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and Final CBS era (December 13, 1951 to June 30, 1952) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Bill Lawrence (director on 4 recordings and transcriber on 3 recordings), Harry Cronman (radio adaptor on 4 recordings), Basil Adlam (music director on 3 recordings), Basil Adlam and His Orchestra (performer on 2 recordings), Bill Davidson (announcer on 2 recordings), [[person|jack-oakie|Jack Oakie]] (performer on 2 recordings), and Joseph Kearns (performer on 2 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.a3129b8eb67efa37|KECA]] (aircheck from station).

A Hollywood anthology in which major film stars performed condensed radio versions of movies and other dramatic stories, with the program closely associated with fundraising for the Motion Picture Relief Fund.

Hollywood dramatic anthology built around condensed performances/adaptations of motion pictures and related dramatic material. GRH contains 364 dated recordings through June 1, 1952.

GRH documents the program through CBS initial era (January 8, 1939 to June 28, 1948) on CBS Radio Network, NBC/Camel era (October 7, 1948 to June 29, 1950) on NBC Radio Network, ABC hour era (September 7, 1950 to May 31, 1951) on ABC Radio Network, and Final CBS era (December 13, 1951 to June 30, 1952) on CBS Radio Network.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Bill Lawrence (director on 4 recordings and transcriber on 3 recordings), Harry Cronman (radio adaptor on 4 recordings), Basil Adlam (music director on 3 recordings), Basil Adlam and His Orchestra (performer on 2 recordings), Bill Davidson (announcer on 2 recordings), Jack Oakie (performer on 2 recordings), and Joseph Kearns (performer on 2 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to ABC Radio Network (broadcast on network), Armed Forces Radio and Television Service (rebroadcast by), CBS Radio Network (broadcast on network), and KECA (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Dixieland music and Quiz shows.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Hollywood film adaptation on network radio, Motion Picture Relief Fund fundraising, and Sponsor and audience shift toward television.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include Lux Radio Theatre (27 shared credited people), Screen Directors Playhouse (17 shared credited people), Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar (12 shared credited people), The Whistler (10 shared credited people), and Academy Award Theater (9 shared credited people).
